findings.question: Q4
findings.title: Single interruption after callback return and before pending registration forgets handed spend
findings.smallest_reproduction: One synthetic dispatch settles run.1. At reader.pinned line 974, 976, or 977, trace raises one KeyboardInterrupt after callback returned. Restore earlier ledger through its native mapping; ordinary gateway.dispatch runs executor a second time.
findings.actual_result: Lines 974/976/977: mapping present in frame locals, callback saw revision 2 versus baseline 1; no pending/unread barrier; executor_calls=2. Lines 978/979 controls: retained spend, executor_calls=1. Unchanged-account controls remain readable.
findings.expected_result: Returned spent account cannot be forgotten by exceptional cleanup and later checkpoint replacement; second executor call refused.
findings.trust_boundary: All owner state changes use public BudgetLedger.settle/from_dict or supported native dictionary replacement. The desk receives a previously admitted synthetic action and invokes its normal executor. Tracing/profiling and temporary helper wrappers schedule failures only; they neither grant authority nor edit reader bookkeeping. Private fields are read only for diagnostics. These are bounded software fault-injection results, not an attacker API or physical validation.
counterarguments: This is not desk-level durable at-most-once: an intervening verification was handed spend, and uninterrupted/late-interrupt controls refuse the same redispatch.
Not the no-handing/failed-callback residual: exact returned mapping is recorded in frame locals.
The source-line injection models an interruption checkpoint, not a measured OS signal timing distribution.
findings.proposed_correction: Initialize a pending-acquisition/result slot before calling accounts and make the exceptional path retain the already returned local mapping even if the ordinary _uncompared registration did not finish. The observed line-974/976/977 variants have a mapping in locals and one interrupt, so a local cleanup repair can capture it before owner control resumes. Do not use handed=True alone as proof of a stored result. This repairs the demonstrated single-interrupt gap, not every repeated capture interruption.

findings.question: Q4
findings.title: Interrupted initial capture and recovery let a raw live mapping erase the original handing
findings.smallest_reproduction: Dispatch once, interrupt native capture and immediate recovery before stable retention, restore ledger through the live dictionary, then dispatch the original admitted action normally.
findings.actual_result: Live dict plus two KeyboardInterrupt, MemoryError, or RecursionError injections: pending=[tuple], unread={}, executor_calls=2. Zero/one failures and detached-dictionary controls: executor_calls=1. Unmodified production functions with trace/profile interruptions at first or second _items map independently reproduce count 2; single-interruption controls count 1. Default-limit native depths 994/995 reproduce raw pending and count 2; depth 993 retains _RetainedHanding and count 1.
findings.expected_result: Recovery must stay bound to originally handed accounts; current replacement contents cannot complete a lost historical comparison.
findings.trust_boundary: All owner state changes use public BudgetLedger.settle/from_dict or supported native dictionary replacement. The desk receives a previously admitted synthetic action and invokes its normal executor. Tracing/profiling and temporary helper wrappers schedule failures only; they neither grant authority nor edit reader bookkeeping. Private fields are read only for diagnostics. These are bounded software fault-injection results, not an attacker API or physical validation.
counterarguments: Helper monkeypatching is not the sole support: production-unmodified trace/profile and native recursion runs corroborate the state transition.
Native recursion alone is not used to override the older explicit stack-exhaustion exclusion; asynchronous probes establish the new lifecycle failure independently.
Detached dictionary control shows raw pending is not always unsafe: its retained entries remain stable there.
Retaining the construction-time account is insufficient: a public replacement before settle leaves the spent object absent from that baseline; this variant also redispatches.
proposed_correction: Retain each completed native mapping/entry capture progressively in the existing pending lifecycle buffer. Failure on the second mapping must not discard a completed first mapping. Canonicalize and reconcile retained account entries with the existing owner rules. This closes the partial-capture loss, but cannot reconstruct an entry never captured.

An explicitly uncaptured observation must not be discharged by rereading a live dictionary as though its present contents were the earlier handoff. A marker can safely refuse temporarily; marker deletion based only on unchanged present content would accept both indistinguishable histories. Keeping it forever would prevent an unchanged honest reader from recovering, so that alone is not a complete fix.

findings.question: Q4
findings.title: Retained raw entry history diverges from owner-normalized unchanged history
findings.smallest_reproduction: Interrupt before _account for a new ordinary charge, then restore the unchanged ledger through BudgetLedger.from_dict and read it.
findings.actual_result: Float/string iteration 1.0/"1", and public BudgetCharge constructor integer realized/from_general_pool fields, permanently diverge only after interruption. Integer iteration and non-interrupted controls recover.
findings.expected_result: Equivalent owner-normalized checkpoint remains usable absent evidence of changed history.
findings.trust_boundary: All owner state changes use public BudgetLedger.settle/from_dict or supported native dictionary replacement. The desk receives a previously admitted synthetic action and invokes its normal executor. Tracing/profiling and temporary helper wrappers schedule failures only; they neither grant authority nor edit reader bookkeeping. Private fields are read only for diagnostics. These are bounded software fault-injection results, not an attacker API or physical validation.
counterarguments: Although iteration is annotated int, public settle accepts the tested spellings and canonical from_dict normalizes them. The constructor integer-cost case also avoids any reliance on string typing.
findings.proposed_correction: Normalize retained BudgetCharge entries through the existing canonical owner read-back path before hashing; keep the exact JSON/default=str behavior used by successful _read_once. Establish the corresponding owner-canonical rule for experiment entries by differential controls. Do not create a competing numeric/history normalization.

findings.question: Q4
findings.title: Two interrupted detached handings falsely retire unchanged content by identity
findings.smallest_reproduction: accounts returns fresh canonical copies of unchanged current ledger. Interrupt _handed once on each of two pins while immediate recovery succeeds; perform normal read afterward.
findings.actual_result: Two detached interruptions permanently set _diverged. One detached interruption and one/two same-object interruptions remain readable.
findings.expected_result: Identity differences of owner-equivalent copies are unresolved until canonical comparison; interruptions alone never prove rewritten history.
findings.trust_boundary: All owner state changes use public BudgetLedger.settle/from_dict or supported native dictionary replacement. The desk receives a previously admitted synthetic action and invokes its normal executor. Tracing/profiling and temporary helper wrappers schedule failures only; they neither grant authority nor edit reader bookkeeping. Private fields are read only for diagnostics. These are bounded software fault-injection results, not an attacker API or physical validation.
counterarguments: This does not require numerical normalization; tested charges are ordinary canonical integer-iteration/float-cost values.
findings.proposed_correction: Keep an identity-mismatched interrupted observation unresolved rather than declaring it rewritten. Reconcile all already-retained alternatives by the owner-canonical history outside the comparison lock, then apply only if the same pending observations still exist. Existing _uncompared can retain them; avoid another authority/evidence vocabulary. Do not permit another callback to overwrite an unresolved barrier.

architecture_assessment.not_a_blanket_impossibility_claim: The observed single-interrupt registration gap, lost first-map capture, numeric normalization and detached reconciliation have local corrections. No implementation fix was made or tested in this read-only review. The argument below concerns any future attempt to recover information after an uncaptured mutable handing has already been replaced; it does not prove that every preventive handoff redesign is impossible.
finite_indistinguishable_histories: Both histories start with the same canonically observed H0 and identical verification sequence. Owner replaces its account with a fresh canonical copy L1, which the reader has never captured.
H_good leaves L1 unchanged. H_spend publicly settles a new charge on L1. Both callbacks return the same kind of live native dictionary.
Two finite pre-first-entry-capture interruptions occur: acquisition and cleanup recovery. Both leave only a raw pair of live dictionaries pending, with no L1 account/entry observation.

Both owners replace the entry with a fresh canonical H0 checkpoint. Interruption then stops. H_good is the unchanged honest restore that must eventually recover; H_spend must refuse H0 because the returned handing held a spend.

The executed comparison records equal reader-observable retained state (seen history, unread/diverged maps, pending map contents, construction-time account content, ticket count, no in-flight tickets, no seal). The L1 weak reference is dead in both cases: the original spend object is no longer retained. Later identical H0 handings cannot distinguish the histories.
architecture_assessment.consequence: Accepting solely from subsequent H0 reads accepts both histories; permanent unresolved refusal blocks both. Additional bounded/arbitrary retries, waiting until interruptions stop, or comparing unchanged present identities/content adds no missing historical information. A new reader silently forgets the timeline and is not an automatic same-reader recovery.

alternatives_examined.alternative: Recover returned mapping in exception handler
alternatives_examined.assessment: Good local fix for family1 when mapping is already stored and recovery completes; a second pre-capture interruption reopens the information-loss state.
Preserves captured portions including E second-map loss, and is worth doing. It cannot reconstruct entries never captured before failure.

Can mitigate caller recursion and selected SIGINT paths; it does not guarantee a snapshot on MemoryError or other allowed interruption, and cannot serialize a live owner replacement without a shared retention/ownership contract.

alternatives_examined.alternative: Retain original account, compare identities, digest current mapping
alternatives_examined.assessment: Public replacement before settle defeats construction-time account retention (executed). Honest detached restore changes identities. Current digest cannot reveal the lost intermediate L1.

alternatives_examined.alternative: Keep unresolved marker forever or automatically reset reader
alternatives_examined.assessment: First preserves safety but violates unchanged honest eventual usability; second restores usability by forgetting observed timeline. Both are contract decisions, not complete transparent fixes.

alternatives_examined.alternative: Owner publishes stable pending handoff before handing and retains it through acknowledgement
alternatives_examined.assessment: Can preserve both requirements without a second budget authority: publish native account-entry snapshot/history owned by execution side, keyed by the existing verification lifecycle, retained across reader interruption until authoritative comparison acknowledges. Requires stable publication and mutation/retention semantics; simply returning a new dictionary is not enough for all mutable experiment containers.

architecture_assessment.precise_decision_required: For an accounts() result whose native entries were never captured, choose the owner contract: (A) require the execution owner to publish and retain a stable handoff/history until the reader acknowledges comparison, permitting eventual recovery after finite interruptions; or (B) explicitly narrow observation to completed stable native capture, documenting pre-capture rollback as unobservable; or (C) permit an unresolved refusal that requires an explicit owner-stated new timeline to recover. B weakens the present returned-handing guarantee; C relaxes same-reader eventual usability. A best preserves the stated invariants. A reader must not silently choose B or C.
architecture_assessment.implementation_boundary: This is a precise acquisition/ownership decision, not an invitation to introduce another scientific budget ledger, execution reservation, evidence vocabulary, or applicability authority.
